chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
When the man is present, use his kunya (teknonym), and when he is absent, use his name.

key_terms.فَسَمِّهِ: so name him (use his given name)

ai.seo_question: What is the proper way to address a man when he is present versus when he is absent according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi establishes a nuanced social protocol where the kunya (e.g., Abu al-Hasan) is used for direct, respectful address in the presence of the individual, while the specific given name is preferred for reference when he is absent. In Shia scholarly tradition, this distinction highlights the balance between immediate honor (kunya) and precise identification (ism), reflecting the high value placed on dignified interpersonal conduct. It serves as a practical guideline for maintaining social harmony and respect in both communal and private contexts.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moammar Bin Khallad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the man was present, so teknonym him, and when he was absent, so name him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad from abu al-Hassan (a.s.) who has said the following: “
When a man is present, call him by his Kunyah (father of so and so) and in his absence call him by his name.”
